title: Target Tools Catalog
description: Canonical catalog of downstream AI-tool targets the compiler emits into the `dist/stacks/<stack>/` tree. This file is both a JSON Schema (it validates the shape of `targets` descriptor objects via the `$defs/TargetDescriptor` sub-schema) AND the live catalog (the 5 canonical descriptors are pinned via `properties.targets.const`). Phase 5 per-tool transformers read this file directly: `json.load(...)['properties']['targets']['const']` returns the canonical list, and each entry tells the transformer what format to emit, where to write it, and how it interacts with source frontmatter flags. Adding a sixth target (e.g., Amazon Q, Windsurf, Codex CLI Memory) is a one-line append to the `const` array PLUS a new transformer module under `compiler/transformers/`.
$comment: Phase 2 deliverable per `docs/02-implementation-plan.md` §5 task 3. The catalog reproduces Architecture Upgrade Report §6.4 (Per-Tool Compilation Variants) verbatim. Note: Memory Bank and ArchUnit are NOT included as targets here because they are stack-level scaffolds, not per-rule opt-ins (they are not boolean fields in `source/**/*.md` frontmatter). They are produced by their own dedicated transformers (`memory_bank_scaffold.py`, generated ArchUnit fixtures in Phase 6) keyed off the stack manifest, not off `target_tools.*`.

targets.description: Array of target descriptors. The compiler iterates this list to discover available transformers and their output contracts. Order is significant only for human readability — the compiler keys lookups by `id`, not by index.

const.notes: Primary distribution target per ADR-0001. Emits one .mdc file per source rule with YAML frontmatter (description, globs, alwaysApply) derived from the source rule's scope.layers and activation.cursor_mode. Cursor reads these natively in 2026 — the legacy .cursorrules format is silently ignored in Agent mode.

Single concatenated Markdown file consumed by GitHub Copilot. The transformer groups source rules by scope.layers and emits an H2 section per layer (## Controller Layer, ## Service Layer, ...). Strips archunit_test and other non-AI-relevant metadata.
Single root-level CLAUDE.md for Claude Code. Same shape as the Copilot output but uses a more directive tone (explicit 'When generating Java code, you MUST...' framing per Phase 5 task 2).

Numbered-list format mirroring JetBrains/junie-guidelines/guidelines/<lang>/<framework>/guidelines.md. Consumed by the JetBrains Junie agent. Output landing path is .junie/AGENTS.md inside the consumer repo.

The cross-tool open standard (OpenAI / Linux Foundation, >60K repos as of Q1 2026). Includes ONLY rules with activation.agents_md_priority == 'high'. Hard cap: 150 lines. If the generated output exceeds 150 lines, the Phase 5 transformer fails the build with a 'demote rules to medium priority' diagnostic. The canonical sections are: Tech Stack, Commands, Code Style, Testing, Boundaries.

TargetDescriptor.description: Shape of a single target-tool descriptor. Adding a new target (Phase 8+) means appending a new object of this shape to `targets.const` PLUS implementing a transformer module under `compiler/transformers/` whose name matches the `id` (with `.py` extension and underscores).

id.description: Stable target identifier (snake_case, lowercase). Must match the key the transformer module is named after AND the `target_tools.<id>` boolean in source-rule frontmatter.

human_name.description: Human-readable name for use in logs and PR descriptions.

format.description: Output file format. `mdc` = Cursor MDC (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body). `markdown` = plain Markdown without frontmatter. `markdown-junie` = JetBrains Junie's numbered-list convention.

output_path_template.description: Path template (Phase-4 transformers expand `{stack}` and `{rule_id}` placeholders). Repository-relative. The `dist/` prefix is added by the compiler driver, NOT by the template.

concatenation_mode.description: `per-rule-file` = each source rule produces one output file (Cursor). `concatenated` = all selected rules are joined into a single output file (Copilot, Claude, Junie, AGENTS.md).

source_frontmatter_flag.description: The dotted path inside source-rule frontmatter that gates emission. The transformer skips any rule where this boolean is `false`. Always of the form `target_tools.<id>`.

supports_globs.description: Whether the target file format supports per-file-pattern activation (true only for Cursor MDC).

supports_alwaysApply.description: Whether the target file format supports an `alwaysApply` style global flag (true only for Cursor MDC).

notes.description: Free-form prose for transformer authors — quirks, format conventions, downstream-consumer expectations.
